concept.name: Wyckoff reaccumulation
concept.definition: A consolidation within an ongoing uptrend in which large operators take profits and acquire additional shares before the markup resumes. Wyckoff described these flat ranges as 'stepping stones' on the way to higher price targets.
concept.intuition: Halfway up the hill, the big players pause to catch their breath and reload, shaking out nervous holders before the next leg higher.
concept.mechanics: A reaccumulation range forms as a sideways pause during markup; its Phase A typically lacks the climactic PS/SC of a primary base and resembles distribution more closely, while Phases B-E are shorter and smaller in amplitude but structurally similar to accumulation. Its point-and-figure count often confirms ('stepping stone confirming count') the target projected from the original base.
relationships: Backup to the edge of the creek
concept.failure_modes: Reaccumulation is easily confused with distribution in real time; a 'stepping stone' that fails to break out upward becomes an ordinary top, and counts from small reaccumulation ranges are less reliable than from primary bases.
concept.misconceptions: A mid-trend consolidation is not automatically reaccumulation; the distinction from distribution is confirmed only by the direction of the eventual resolution and the price-volume character of the range.
concept.example: A stock that doubled off its base trades sideways for eight weeks on falling volume, then breaks out; the analyst's count from this smaller range points to roughly the same target as the original base count, confirming it as reaccumulation.

citations.source: The Wyckoff Method: A Tutorial (StockCharts.com ChartSchool, by Roman Bogomazov and Michael Lipsett)
